Priyom —

Thanks for sending these through. Quick answers up-front:
- We do need the UK Addendum language; our UK entities will require it for any processing of personal data.
- We have a small set of data that is PHI-adjacent (clinical trial identifiers and provider notes) — treating as sensitive. We’d like a firm commitment on routing and encryption controls, or to scope that data into a private-hosting plan.

A couple of clarifying questions on the redline:
1) In your DPA §3.2 the phrase "limited cross-border egress unless agreed" — can you clarify how that works operationally? Will we be able to pin data to EU-only nodes?
2) For SCCs: are you proposing the 2021 modules or a hybrid? Our legal prefers the 2021 set but also an explicit reference to supplementary measures for cloud providers.

We’re looping in Samir (CC’d) from our privacy team and our procurement lead will be J. Patel (I’ll introduce separately). Could you put Laura on an email confirming the proposed fallback language for roles and whether Redwood will accept a processor-only role with limited controller obligations for data routing?

Team / Marta —

Thanks — I reviewed the MSA redline and the DPA draft. Below are recommended positions and a short playbook for the next call. I’ve attached a clean DPA with tracked high-risk language and an SCCs comparison workbook for your review (SCCs-comparison.xlsx).

Key legal positions we can take:
1) SCCs: Redwood will accept the 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses (modules for controller-processor where applicable). We propose to add a short Supplementary Measures paragraph referencing encryption in transit & at-rest, key access controls, and contractual proof of subprocessor controls. (See DPA §5(b) in attached document.)
2) Roles: Redwood will accept processor status for hosting and inference pipelines. However, we need limited controller-like obligations where Orchid requires routing constraints (e.g., pinning to EU region). We propose language that allows Orchid to specify "geofencing requirements" in the order form; Redwood will implement as a configuration subject to agreed-on capacity & cost. (Proposed clause in DPA §2.1.a.)
3) PHI/sensitive data: For any PHI-scope data, we recommend a private deployment addendum (Private Deployment Addendum — PDA) or explicit order-form checkbox that triggers VPC/private-hosting SLA and KMS integration. This will carry a pricing delta and a deployment lead time (2–4 weeks typical).
4) Transfer-impact: We propose a limited-transfer addendum that enumerates permitted export regions and requires notice for new regions >30 days. This reduces surprise for both sides and gives procurement time for approvals.

Evidence & operations items we need from Orchid before legal sign-off:
- Confirm list of hosting accounts/regions and any contractual UK entity names.
- Data inventory that flags PHI-adjacent categories (sample CSV acceptable).
- Procurement/PO contact for order-form modifications.

Proposed MAP for negotiation:
- Day 0: Accept DPA baseline (Redwood proposes SCCs 2021 + supplementary measures).
- Day 3: Joint call with privacy + ops to walk hosting constraints and PHI scope.
- Day 7: Redwood provides PDA pricing estimate and updated redlines.
- Day 14: Target for order-form signoff or escalate procurement blockers.

I’ll attach: DPA-proposed-redlines.docx (clean copy with annotated comments), SCCs-comparison.xlsx. Ben, please confirm implementation feasibility on geofencing and an estimate for private-hosting lead time & cost delta so I can include numbers in the MAP.

Laura Bennett
